title: What If We Covered the Sahara in Solar and Wind Farms?

scenes.text: What if we covered the Sahara in solar and wind farms? Computer models say it would rain.
A 2018 study in Science modeled huge wind and solar farms there. Desert rainfall more than doubled.
In the Sahel to the south, rain rose 200 to 500 millimeters a year.
Plant cover grew about 20 percent. More plants hold more moisture, which brings more rain.
The authors say such farms could in principle replace today's fossil fuel energy.
It's only a model. But the best case turns a desert into a power plant, and a garden.
